name: BACH_0081
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Invasive (100%)** · Confident · Careful review
Single-class conformal set and MUSK agreement, but only 2 of 5 similar cases are invasive [F5].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Invasive >99%, InSitu <1% | Very high |
| Conformal set | {Invasive} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 1.00 / 88th percentile | Input reliable |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes, same top class | Agrees |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Invasive | Weak support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 6, 10, 11) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; concept model links it to invasion [F2] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 5, 8, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; concept model links it to lower invasive likelihood · Weak
- **Immune cells near tumor** (regions 0, 2, 10) · context · Higher than 92% of reference images; sampled regions only [F7] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Effect vs random is 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007); not shown to reflect classifier use. TILs (8/20) is Weak.

## Could be wrong if
- The 3 InSitu neighbors are right and this is in-situ disease, not invasion.
- Gland formation in regions 8, 9 (25–40% invasive each) reflects benign or in-situ glands.

## Check on the slide
1. **6, 10, 11**: Confirm tumor cells infiltrate stroma rather than benign fibrous stroma.
2. **8, 9**: Low per-region scores with gland formation: benign glands or invasive tubules?
3. **0, 7**: Region 0: in-situ duct component? Region 7: confirm necrosis, mitoses, TILs by eye.
